Separately, the tentative US-Iran de-escalation has reversed: US forces struck five Iranian oil tankers linked to the IRGC in the Gulf of Oman after a second Iranian missile attack on a US Navy warship in three days (the missiles missed the vessel), fueling fears of increasingly sophisticated Iranian weapons and pushing oil prices toward $100 a barrel. This marks a sharp escalation from earlier signs of thaw, including Trump's claim that Hormuz mines were cleared and the State Department's restaffing of evacuated Middle East posts. Iran continues to denounce US sanctions as 'gross lawlessness,' China warns of retaliation while urging ceasefire, and Pakistan continues mediation efforts.

Separately, it has emerged that Harry and Meghan withdrew their children Archie and Lilibet from a new private UK school after just two days, after their protective convoy became separated in heavy traffic during the school run on the first day of term. Meanwhile, King Harald V of Norway was laid to rest in Oslo, concluding 13 days of national mourning, with Prince William leading the UK delegation and world leaders including Spain's King Felipe, Princess Anne, and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy attending; Zelenskyy's plane was reportedly nearly struck by a drone shortly after departing Moldova. William also made a surprise public appearance with Catherine at Everton's stadium to launch a new suicide prevention campaign. Separately, a public feud has escalated between King Charles and Princess Diana's brother, Earl Charles Spencer, after Spencer's memoir 'Swan Song: Diana, My Sister' alleged Charles told him days after Diana's 1997 death that she would 'be forgotten soon enough,' and that Charles sounded 'giddily elated, like a lottery winner' in a phone call after her death; Spencer also claims some Palace staff were 'relieved' at Diana's death and details a dispute over the coffin procession arrangements. As the memoir's Daily Mail serialisation continues, new claims have emerged: that Queen Elizabeth offered to restore Diana's HRH title after her death, and that Diana told Spencer 'my husband is in love with his valet' before disclosing plans to divorce Charles. Buckingham Palace issued a rare public rebuttal, breaking its 'never complain, never explain' tradition, while insider reports describe Prince William as 'furious' and King Charles's anger over the claims as immense. Prince Harry said he was 'aware' of the book's contents. Amid the row, William and Catherine visited Rothesay on the Isle of Bute while King Charles attended an AI summit at Dumfries House, which was overshadowed by the memoir controversy.

facts.state_of_play: Trump reports progress on establishing a permanent US military base in Poland, with a location announcement expected soon. Polish PM Tusk warns that Russia may deliberately or accidentally strike NATO allies, and Western intelligence reportedly indicates Putin is planning a missile strike on a NATO country to test the alliance's resolve, after a Russian attack near western Ukraine forced Poland to close its airspace and scramble fighter jets. Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics has separately warned that Europe is not keeping pace with rapidly evolving drone and aerial warfare in Ukraine, saying most NATO states could not repel a Russian missile attack if the war expands. French President Emmanuel Macron says Russian hybrid attacks against Europe are intensifying and has ordered protection of French infrastructure and defence industry sites, while also calling for an emergency G7 meeting to address soaring energy prices amid the Ukraine and Middle East wars. On the ground, Russia has struck Ukraine's border crossings with Poland and Moldova and its drones are threatening Western officials traveling to Kyiv, even as its eastern offensive appears to be stalling. Separately, Ukraine and Russia are reportedly growing frustrated with US envoy Steve Witkoff and the US-mediated peace process, though Trump is said to see no problem with Witkoff's role. Meanwhile, Russia has begun a three-day parliamentary election - the first since its 2022 invasion of Ukraine - with only parties supporting the war allowed on the ballot; United Russia, which won more than two-thirds of seats in 2021, is expected to retain its dominance amid signs of economic strain among voters, and has used celebrities like NHL star Alex Ovechkin in its campaign. Separately, Latvia has imposed an indefinite entry ban on Ovechkin and sanctioned oligarch Umar Kremlev, a close Putin associate who also has financial ties to Donald Trump Jr. Amid Republican criticism over the propriety of Trump Jr. accepting a lavish Bahamas wedding party from Kremlev, Trump Jr. has repaid Kremlev for the party, and President Trump has publicly defended the arrangement, calling such gifts common.
